reason: The cited evidence does not address W–Cu composites, Ni coatings as diffusion barriers, or thermal conductivity under irradiation. E1 discusses TiC in W, E2 describes Ti/Ni coatings on diamond in a HEA matrix, and E3 concerns Mg alloy composites. None of the key premises are supported by the provided passages.
premises: A thin Ni coating can be applied conformally to W particles or ligaments before consolidation.
The Ni interlayer acts as a diffusion barrier that reduces interdiffusion between W and Cu.
The Ni interlayer mitigates thermal expansion mismatch and stabilizes the interface against void formation.
Reduced interfacial voids and phase separation lead to higher effective thermal conductivity.
The coating approach is effective under ~350°C and ion irradiation relevant to plasma-facing joints.
